CexCellView.description: One register's concrete value in a counterexample state.

CounterexampleView.description: D1.8b — a stall-lasso counterexample for the API (mirrors `ExactCounterexample`): reset → `prefix` → repeating `cycle`, each state an ordered list of register cells.

cycle.description: The repeating stall cycle; the last state steps back to `cycle[0]`.

inputs.description: P3 / mununu#536 — the per-cycle INPUT assignment that drives the trace, so the counterexample can be replayed against the RTL. Present on the core report all along; both wire shapes dropped it, which made a trace readable but not runnable.

prefix.description: States from the reset state up to (excluding) the cycle entry.

unreachable_target.description: A.4 — for a `Violated` bare `EF p` (reachability): the target predicate atoms that are UNREACHABLE from reset ("the design never reaches these"). Empty for the stall-lasso / trap-path (liveness) counterexamples, which carry `prefix`/`cycle`.

ExpectationFailureView.description: mununu#537 — one unmet claim. `property` is absent for a run-level claim (the count).

ExpectationResultView.description:
mununu#537 — the verdict on a caller's declared expectations.

`satisfied: false` corresponds to CLI exit code **4** — "a verdict was not what you claimed", deliberately distinct from a failed run (1) and from the ordinary verdict gate (2 / 3).

auto_provided_stubs.description: Cut flop-primitive modules for which a behavioral stub was auto-injected so the register survives the lift (e.g. `prim_sparse_fsm_flop`).

blackboxed_modules.description: Modules instantiated without a body, cut to free inputs (registers they drive are not modeled as state). Empty for a self-contained design.

config_values.description: mununu#536 — config inputs pinned for this run, each `"<signal>=<value>"`. A verdict under a pin is a claim about THAT configuration only, so the scope ships with it.

cutpoints.description: mununu#536 — signals cut to free inputs by `--cutpoint`: the control slice these verdicts were reached under.

frontend.description: `"read_verilog + sv2v"`, `"yosys-slang (read_slang)"`). `--frontend auto` picks one silently and the two paths differ in SOUNDNESS on partial writes (#464/#465), so "which lift produced this verdict?" is a question the payload must answer. It was previously reachable only as `lift-frontend` note prose.
frontend.title: 466 / mununu#536 — the RTL front end that produced the lift (e.g.

frontend_fallback_reason.description: attempt's error. `None` when there was no fallback.
frontend_fallback_reason.title: 466 — when `--frontend auto` FELL BACK (an earlier front end errored), the prior

gated_resets.description: Reset inputs pinned inactive at the model level (`"<signal>=<value>"`), with their `disable iff` guards dropped from the formulas. Empty when reset-gating is off or no `disable iff` reset was recognized.

state_register_count.description: Number of state register lines in the lifted model.

counterexample.description: D1.8b — a concrete stall-lasso counterexample, present only for a Violated bare `AF p` decided by the exact engine (`engine: "exact-symbolic"`).

detail.description:
Human-readable detail: `"N cell(s)"` (violated/unknown) or the skip reason.

**Prefer the structured fields below.** This is prose and stays only so existing consumers keep working; a gate that needs the figure should read `false_cells` / `unknown_cells` / `skip_reason` rather than parsing this string.

false_cells.description: mununu#536 — the cell count behind a `violated` verdict, machine-readable. `None` for every other outcome.

seeded_predicates.description: The cube predicates auto-seeded for this property (atom strings).

skip_reason.description: mununu#536 — why a `skipped` property was not evaluated. `None` for every other outcome.

unknown_cells.description:
mununu#536 — the cell count behind an `unknown` (⊥) verdict, machine-readable. `None` for every other outcome.

This is the "cell/budget figure that accompanies a ⊥" the issue asks for: a ⊥ is a statement about how much of the cube space stayed undecided, and a consumer tracking whether refinement is helping needs the number, not a sentence containing it.

UnsupportedAssertionView.description: An assertion outside the supported fragment (mirrors `UnsupportedAssertion`).

detail.description: Longer explanation (the why + the soundness/scope implication).

diagnostics.description: Model-level diagnostics: state-register count + black-boxed (cut) modules. Lets a SKIPPED outcome point at its root cause.

expectations.description:
mununu#537 — the result of checking this run against the caller's declared expectations. `None` (and omitted) when no expectations were declared, in which case the ordinary verdict gate applies.

Present so a consumer learns **which** claim failed without parsing prose.

notes.description: H.J — human-facing provenance notes: every abstraction / scoping decision the run made (config concretizations, reset-gating, flop stubs, cut modules, the abstraction posture, the coverage summary), so a verdict's scope and caveats are explicit in the payload.

unsupported.description: Assertions that did not translate (reuses the extract-sva view shape; `kind` is `None` here).
